The '''2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team''' represented [[Duke University]] during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Blue Devils were led by second-year head coach [[Jon Scheyer]]. The Blue Devils played their home games at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]], as a member of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].

The Blue Devils started the season ranked second in the nation, and dominated [[2023–24 Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball team|Dartmouth]] in their season opener. The schedule became more difficult as they lost by four points to twelfth-ranked [[2023–24 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]]. They followed the loss with a defeat of eighteenth-ranked [[2023–24 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in the [[Champions Classic]]. They went on to win three straight games before losing at [[2023–24 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]]. They were defeated by [[2023–24 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] by four points in their ACC opener. After back-to-back defeats, the Blue Devils went on to win eight straight games. This included wins over tenth-ranked [[2023–24 Baylor Bears men's basketball team|Baylor]] and a defeat over Georgia Tech to avenge the previous loss. The winning streak was broken with a four-point loss to [[2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]]. They won their next three games before a [[Carolina–Duke rivalry|rivalry]] matchup with [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. North Carolina won by nine points, but the Blue Devils would win their next five straight games. Duke lost two of its last five games, with one of the losses coming at in-state rival [[2023–24 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] and the other being a final-day loss to North Carolina.

The Blue Devils finished the season 27–9 and 15–5 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in second place. As the second seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they earned a bye to the quarterfinals, where they were upset by in-state rival and tenth-seed [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2024 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]], where they were the 4th seed in the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#South regional – Dallas, Texas|South]] Region. They faced [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball|Vermont]] in the First Round. They won this matchup to move on to the round of 32, where they routed 12th seed [[James Madison Dukes men's basketball|James Madison]]. Duke then faced the number one seed, [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], whom they defeated 54–51, advancing to the Elite Eight for the first time under head coach Jon Scheyer. There, they were once again upset by 11th-seeded NC State to end their season.

== Previous season ==
The [[2022–23 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Blue Devils]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 27–9, 14–6 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for third place. As the No. 4 seed in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they defeated [[2022–23 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]], [[2022–23 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]], and [[2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] to win the tournament championship. The championship was their 22nd [[ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] victory in program history. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 5 seed in the East region. There, they defeated [[2022–23 Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Oral Roberts]] before losing in the second round to [[2022–23 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]].
